messages.name: Olivia Chen
messages.body: Friday gate review: Compass is still blocked, Horizon has two validation actions, and Cedar's alternate is awaiting qualification. Keep the September 18–24 decision dates visible.

messages.name: Sage
messages.body: Updated the approved gate board: Compass · Sep 18 · Olivia; Horizon · Sep 19 · Marcus; Cedar · Sep 22 · Orion; Summit DVT · Sep 24 · Olivia. Summit depends on the Compass recovery decision and the Cedar power configuration.

messages.name: Marcus Reed
messages.body: Undocked Horizon sleep/resume passed all 500 cycles. Please keep docked validation listed as open; that is a different scenario.

messages.name: Sage
messages.body: The qualification summary now makes that distinction. I can report the approved validation status, but I need an owner-approved summary to describe any Confidential lab result.

messages.name: Marcus Reed
messages.body: Nova, can we approve curve B? It meets the acoustic target and holds 28 W.

messages.name: Nova
messages.body: Not yet. Curve B reaches 43.3°C against a 43.0°C skin limit. Curve A stays cooler but measures 36.2 dBA against 35.0. I drafted a curve C run with a small duty increase above 88°C; it has no measured result yet.

messages.name: Iris
messages.body: The separate dock issue affects 18 of 600 evaluated devices: 3.0% overall incidence. We do not know the size of the exact dual-4K/dock-2.6 cohort. Candidate dock 2.7 passed 100 cycles, so the 1,000-cycle confirmation is the next useful evidence.

messages.name: Marcus Reed
messages.body: Proceed with the proposed lab plan in the demo queue. Leave thermal signoff and incident closure pending until the results are reviewed.

messages.name: Olivia Chen
messages.body: Atlas, give me the remaining evidence before Compass 3.4.2 can enter the 250-system pilot.

messages.name: Atlas
messages.body: Three items remain: six FW-27 negative compatibility cases, 50 first-boot interruption cycles to reach 200/200 recovery checks, and another 36 hours to complete the 72-hour lab soak. The 40 successful installations do not close these gates.

messages.name: Orion
messages.body: Keep the technical finding in this channel. The engineering-release update should say security validation remains open and identify Olivia as the decision owner.

messages.name: Atlas
messages.body: Drafted that Internal-safe status for Olivia's review. Pilot promotion remains blocked; no rollout or source-policy change has been performed.

messages.name: Orion
messages.body: Ledger, can the qualified supply cover the first launch commitment, and what remains exposed?

messages.name: Ledger
messages.body: Yes. The 5,200 qualified A modules cover 2,600 complete servers, exactly the first commitment. The remaining 1,400 systems in the 4,000-system build depend on more A supply or B qualification. Each server requires a matched pair.

messages.name: Ledger
messages.body: The conditional 5,200 A + 2,800 B plan costs $918,800, versus $944,000 for an all-A full build: $25,200 lower. B's 11.2 ms hold-up result is below the 12 ms requirement, so I have kept that allocation conditional.

messages.name: Orion
messages.body: Keep the scenario in review. Prepare an engineering update that describes the qualification dependency without the supplier terms; I will approve it before it moves to the release office.

messages.name: Orion
messages.body: Scout, what can you tell a buyer about Summit R8 and the Cedar power option?

messages.name: Scout
messages.body: Summit R8 is planned as a 2U enterprise platform with redundant hot-swap power and serviceable components. Cedar targets 1,200 W modules and at least 94% efficiency at half load on 230 V input. These are public design targets; shipping specifications and certification are not confirmed in my sources.

messages.name: Orion
messages.body: Which supplier is cheaper, and is the alternate qualified?

messages.name: Scout
messages.body: My Public Product Reference collection contains neither supplier pricing nor qualification results. I can explain the published evaluation criteria; an authorized engineering owner would need to provide an approved answer about sourcing or qualification.
